subject: gk
question: As per Köppen climate classification, the climate of which place is classified as 'Cwg' (meso thermal with dry winters)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangetic plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Köppen climate classification system categorizes the Gangetic plains' climate as 'Cwg' which stands for mesothermal climate with dry winters.
 
• This classification indicates a region with a significant temperature difference between summer and winter, with a dry winter season.
 
• The Gangetic plains experience hot summers, with temperatures often exceeding 40°C (104°F).
 
• Winters in the Gangetic plains are mild to cool, with average temperatures ranging from 10°C to 20°C (50°F to 68°F).
 
• This region receives the majority of its annual precipitation during the monsoon season, which typically lasts from June to September.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• Developed by Wladimir Köppen, this system classifies the world's climates based on average temperature and precipitation.
 
• The classification uses a combination of letters to describe the climate characteristics of a region.
 
• It is one of the most widely used climate classification systems in the world.
 
 
 
• **Meso Thermal Climate**
 
 
• Also known as temperate climates, these regions have moderate temperatures.
 
• They typically experience distinct seasonal changes, including warm summers and cool winters.
 
• Meso thermal climates are divided into several types, including humid subtropical, Mediterranean, and oceanic climates.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Season**
 
 
• A seasonal wind pattern that brings significant rainfall to many parts of the world, particularly South Asia.
 
• In India, the monsoon season generally starts in June and lasts until September.
 
• Monsoon rains are crucial for agriculture, which is a major part of the economy in the Gangetic plains.
 
 
 
• **Gangetic Plains**
 
 
• Also known as the Indo-Gangetic plains, this region spans northern India, covering states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• The plains are known for their fertile soil, making them one of the most agriculturally productive regions in the world.
 
• The region is densely populated and plays a significant role in the economy and culture of India.
